prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1116; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by the third-party vehicle. Police report obtained. Insured reports no fault concerns and provided a photo of the rear bumper damage. Third-party driver's carrier notified and liability acceptance requested.

Entry 2: Claimant reported neck and shoulder pain at the scene and was transported to urgent care. Claimant has now retained counsel, who has requested that all further communication be directed to the firm. Letter of representation received and placed in file. Future contact with claimant suspended pending counsel's instructions.

Entry 3: Vehicle inspection completed at the body shop. Damage estimate reviewed and found consistent with the reported impact. Rear bumper, trunk lid, and tail light assembly identified for replacement. Repair authorization issued. Rental vehicle arranged for the insured for the expected repair period.

Entry 4: Counsel's office submitted medical records and a treatment summary for the claimant's shoulder injury. Records show initial diagnosis of a rotator cuff strain, followed by physical therapy and a referral for imaging. Medical bills itemized and under review. Requested an independent medical review to confirm the reasonableness and relatedness of the treatment plan.

Entry 5: Demand package received from counsel with supporting medical documentation and wage loss records. Claim file referred to the bodily injury unit for valuation review. Liability position confirmed with the third-party carrier, which has accepted responsibility for the collision. Reserves adjusted to reflect the pending injury evaluation. Next step is to schedule a settlement conference with counsel.
